name: Sthalasayana Perumal Temple, Thirukkadalmallai
deity: Vishnu as Sthalasayana Perumal, reclining on the bare earth, with the Goddess Nilamangai Thayar
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar and Bhoothathalvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Pallava origins, with later Chola, Vijayanagara and Nayak additions
summary: In the seaside town of Mamallapuram, Vishnu rests directly on the earth as Sthalasayana Perumal — a living Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu and the reputed birthplace of Bhoothathalvar.

sections.history: Thirukkadalmallai is the old Tamil name of Mamallapuram, and this is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; it belongs to Thondai Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar offered twenty-six pasurams here and Bhoothathalvar one, twenty-seven in all, and the shrine is believed to be the birthplace of Bhoothathalvar, whose own small shrine stands near the tank opposite the temple. The temple is believed to have been raised by the Pallavas, with later contributions from the medieval Cholas, the Vijayanagara kings and the Madurai Nayaks. It is a living place of worship in the town, distinct from the famed UNESCO-inscribed monuments of Mamallapuram.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian tradition and added to by successive dynasties, the temple is entered through a gateway and gathers around the sanctum of Sthalasayana Perumal, with the Goddess Nilamangai Thayar worshipped as his consort. In the sanctum the sage Pundarika is shown standing beside the lord. Opposite the temple lies its sacred tank, the Pundarika Pushkarini, named for the sage, and near it stands the shrine of Bhoothathalvar. The deity's posture, reclining on the ground rather than on the serpent Adishesha, is the shrine's distinguishing feature.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Pundarika, who gathered lotuses to offer to Vishnu reposing on the Milk Ocean and, in his devotion, set about emptying the sea to reach him. Vishnu came to him as an old man and sent the sage off to fetch food. When Pundarika returned, he found the lord reclining on the bare ground, and so he is worshipped here as Sthalasayana — he who lies upon the earth. The name Thirukkadalmallai is remembered as recalling the sea and this tale.
sections.festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi is the great observance of the year, when devotees gather before dawn for the opening of the northern gateway. The birth-star festival of Bhoothathalvar is celebrated with special worship at the temple and at his shrine by the tank. Confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: Few Divya Desams sit so close to the sea. Come to see Vishnu at rest upon the earth itself, then walk to the Pundarika Pushkarini and the small shrine of Bhoothathalvar opposite. The lord's humble posture invites quiet, unhurried darshan, and the temple stands apart from the sightseeing crowds elsewhere in the town.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Mamallapuram, on the East Coast Road about 55 km south of Chennai, reached by road from Chennai or Chengalpattu. The nearest major rail junction is Chengalpattu, and the nearest airport is Chennai.
